title: Platform Brief: SaaS GTM — Inference Value Metrics & Battlecards
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose: This brief consolidates product positioning, high-impact value metrics, competitive battlecards, pricing guidance, a compact case study, and a prospect-facing security FAQ tailored for SaaS platform buyers evaluating LLM inference solutions. Audience: AEs, SEs, solutions engineers, and product marketing running discovery and technical evaluation calls with mid-market and enterprise SaaS buyers.

Executive positioning (one-liner)

Redwood Inference: Predictable, production-grade LLM inference that maximizes performance and minimizes unit cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — giving platform teams a single API and operational surface to ship reliable AI features without rebuilding inference infrastructure.

Top 3 buyer outcomes we lead with

- Reduce per-inference cost while keeping sub-100ms tail latency for common interactive flows.
- Move from prototype to SLA-backed production without re-architecting (same API for hosted, reserved, and private).
- De-risk compliance through private deployment and audit-friendly telemetry.

Key value metrics and how to frame them in discovery

- Latency (P95/P99): Typical hosted P95 for chat flows: 80–180ms (short prompts, <256 tokens). P99 target for Dedicated: <250ms. Discuss tail-latency SLOs and fallback routing to smaller quantized models for spikes.
- Throughput: Batch-aware throughput gains: 2–6x cost savings for high-concurrency embedding jobs with batching & caching. Ask about queries/sec (QPS) and average request size.
- Cost per 1k prompt tokens: Provide customer-specific model/quantization comps. Example framing: "Switching from single-instance self-host to Redwood Dedicated saved AcornCRM ~48% per-token on standard 8K-chat workload."
- Availability / SLA: Hosted: 99.9% regional uptime; Dedicated: 99.95% backed by contract. Use these to quantify expected downtime impact on revenue ops.
- Time-to-production: Typical onboarding (hosted) = 1–3 days; Dedicated proof-of-concept = 2–4 weeks (infra & capacity provisioning).

Battlecard: Primary competitors and how to position

- Cloud-managed endpoints (Hyperscaler-managed LLM endpoints)
  - Strengths: deep cloud integration, single-provider billing.
  - Redwood advantage: Superior latency predictability, multi-model catalog (open models + tuned variants), and lower unit cost via continuous batching, quantization profiles, and model routing policies.
  - Messaging: "Like managed endpoints, but tuned for inference economics and predictable tail latency for production apps."

- LLM API providers (simple hosted APIs)
  - Strengths: easy dev experience, low time-to-value.
  - Redwood advantage: Matches dev ergonomics but adds Dedicated / Private lanes and enterprise controls (VPC, KMS, audit logs) so customers don’t have to replatform as they scale.
  - Messaging: "From prototype to SLA-backed production without rewriting your integration."

- Self-hosted inference stacks (open-source runtime + infra)
  - Strengths: maximum control, on-prem fit for regulated data.
  - Redwood advantage: We provide a hardened runtime, autoscaling, cost controls, and rollout tooling—plus optional on-prem packaging and a customer-managed control plane for compliance. Lower TCO for teams that value operational simplicity and performance tuning.
  - Messaging: "Get the benefits of a maintained, optimized inference runtime without hiring a deep infra team."

Pricing guidance (rules of thumb for AEs to use in discovery)

- Pricing levers to highlight: model family, instance type (Dedicated SKU), quantization tier, reserved commit vs burst, embedding vs generative unit pricing.
- Proposal archetypes:
  - Self-serve hosted starter: no commit, pay-as-you-go per-token and per-embedding. Ideal for product/feature proofs.
  - Dedicated entry: 3–6 month reserved capacity (monthly commit), includes capacity reservation, 24/7 priority support, and model access. Typical for midmarket customers expecting consistent QPS.
  - Private Deployment: fixed platform fee + per-node license + premium support and compliance bundle. For regulated customers or those requiring air-gapped environments.

- Example customer scenario (SaaS search & assistant) — ballpark illustration to use during commercial conversations:
  - Baseline: 3M tokens / month, predominantly generation (average 500 tokens/session), 2M embeddings / month.
  - Hosted cost estimate (pay-as-you-go): $6,000–$9,000 / month depending on model family and streaming usage.
  - Dedicated cost estimate (reserved): $3,200–$5,500 / month equivalent (with 12-month commit) — includes better latency SLAs and lower per-token unit economics.
  - Use these numbers as conversation starters and include precise model-match quotes from pricing desk for final proposals.

Pitch deck outline (6 slides, one-line purpose each)

1. Problem: Rising inference costs, tail latency, and operational debt when scaling LLM features.
2. Vision & Value: Unified inference runtime with predictable economics and deployment flexibility.
3. Product: Redwood product map (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize).
4. Proof points: Performance benchmarks (P95/P99 numbers), cost comparisons vs self-host & hyperscalers, and a short case study.
5. Security & compliance: VPC, KMS integrations, SOC2 / ISO posture, audit logs, and private deployment options.
6. Commercials & next steps: Pricing archetypes, pilot offer, success criteria and timeline.

Compact case study: AcornCRM (SaaS CRM) — 8-week engagement

- Situation: AcornCRM needed a contextual assistant for sales reps with sub-200ms P95 latency and tight data residency constraints for EU customers. Their prototype used a mix of self-hosted models and occasional hyperscaler endpoints.
- Action: Redwood onboarded AcornCRM to Hosted API for an initial pilot (2 weeks), instrumented prompt caching and prefix KV caching, then migrated them to a Dedicated pool with quantized model variants for EU traffic. Provided rollout plan with canary and automatic fallback policies.
- Results: 
  - Latency: P95 from ~420ms to 160ms after Dedicated + batching optimizations.
  - Cost: Estimated per-token unit cost reduced 48% vs their previous single-instance hosting baseline.
  - Reliability: Achieved 99.96% uptime for critical inference routes over 90 days.
- Quote (paraphrased): "We launched our assistant into production faster than expected and kept response times consistent across our EU and US customers — the cost reduction was material to our unit economics." — Head of Platform, AcornCRM

Security FAQ for prospects (short and direct)

Q: Can Redwood run in my VPC / on-prem?
A: Yes. We offer Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. Contact sales for deployment checklist and lead time (typically 4–8 weeks depending on network & hardware).

Q: How is customer data protected in Hosted?
A: Data is encrypted in-transit (TLS 1.2+) and at-rest (AES-256). Optional per-customer keying via KMS (bring-your-own-key supported on Dedicated & Private). We retain only transient inference artifacts by default; retention is configurable.

Q: Do you have third-party attestations?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence; customers with enterprise contracts can request evidence under NDA.

Q: How are audit logs surfaced?
A: Redwood Console exposes request-level telemetry, per-token cost breakdowns, model version, and an audit trail for administrative actions. Logs can also be forwarded to your SIEM via secure forwarding.

Q: What controls exist to prevent data leakage in model updates?
A: Model onboarding and updates are gated by the model-onboarding team. We sign model-change notices and provide canary/eval runs tied to your evaluation suites. Private deployments allow complete model binaries under customer control.

Q: How do you handle incident response and notifications?
A: We maintain a documented incident process with dedicated SRE on-call rotation. Customers with Dedicated or Private get a designated technical account lead (TAL) and a post-incident report within 72 hours for Sev1 incidents.

Objection handling snippets (short scripts for SEs/AEs)

- "We can build this ourselves": Ask about the cost of hiring/retaining ops talent, time-to-first-SLA, and the ongoing tuning effort. Offer a TCO comparison and pilot to prove the economics.
- "We need data to stay on-prem": Lead with Private deployment and provide the deployment checklist + typical timelines.
- "Hyperscaler pricing is better": Request concrete usage patterns and offer a model-by-model cost comparison; emphasize predictable tail latency and the operational burden of maintaining tuning and rollout tooling.

Success criteria and pilot checklist (what we want to validate in a POC)

- Business/technical success criteria (mutually agreed): target P95 latency, acceptable per-token cost delta vs prototype, error rate threshold (<0.5% request errors), and integration completion (SDK + tracing).
- Technical deliverables: sample prompt set, representative traffic replay (1–3 days), evaluation prompts for quality checks, production routing plan, and SLO definition.
- Timeline (typical):
  - Week 0: Kickoff, secret exchange, and prompt set delivery.
  - Week 1–2: Hosted pilot, instrumentation, perf tuning.
  - Week 3–4: Dedicated provisioning (if applicable), canary rollout.
  - Week 4–8: Stabilization, cost tuning, and handoff to platform/ops.
